events.continuity_hook: Keep the selected Saturday-through-Friday flights, the Coronado suite and confirmed sleeping arrangement, complete airfare and lodging totals, breakfast inclusion, cancellation deadline, airport transfer estimate, and planned zoo and waterfront travel times together as the booked family trip.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck the three traveler names, flight dates, suite occupancy, taxes, and cancellation terms, then book the flights and hotel if the totals remain accurate.
events.scenario_brief: The Coronado property has confirmed that the sofa bed can be prepared for Marcus's son and that the quoted suite rate covers all three guests. Its included breakfast and lack of a nightly resort charge now put it close to the Mission Bay room's complete six-night cost, while the Saturday outbound and Friday return flights remain available at the previously compared times.

events.continuity_hook: Retain the booked Coronado suite, altered nonstop arrival, earlier nonstop fare difference and seats for three, connecting itinerary and transfer time, airport-to-hotel estimates, and the effect of each option on the first evening.
events.interaction_goal: Compare accepting the later arrival with paying for the earlier nonstop or taking the connection, and update the flights only if another option meaningfully restores the first evening.
events.scenario_brief: The airline has moved the family's Saturday arrival 95 minutes later, reducing the time available before dinner but leaving the six-night stay intact. An earlier nonstop is available for an additional amount per traveler, while a similarly priced connecting option arrives near the original time but introduces a tight transfer for the family.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the accepted flight times and seats, hotel confirmation and late check-in note, checked-bag arrival estimate, shuttle pickup window, rideshare range, and realistic hotel arrival time as the final first-night plan.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm that no airline or hotel action is pending, choose workable airport transportation, and record the arrival sequence for all three travelers.
events.scenario_brief: With departure approaching, the family has retained the rescheduled nonstop and their seats remain together. The hotel has confirmed late check-in, but advance airport transportation quotes vary sharply because their arrival overlaps with a large downtown event; the least expensive shuttle has a fixed pickup window that may be too close to baggage claim.

events.continuity_hook: Carry the viable Monday evening arrivals, Tuesday review time and location, Columbus-to-Cincinnati drive estimate, Wednesday inspection window, round-trip and open-jaw airfare totals, and two practical Wednesday return times into the hotel and car comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the round-trip and open-jaw structures against both work appointments and select the schedule to use for complete trip pricing without purchasing.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus needs to attend a Tuesday morning district review in Columbus and a Wednesday afternoon restaurant opening check in Cincinnati. A round trip through Columbus is less expensive but requires driving back after the second appointment, while flying into Columbus and home from Cincinnati shortens Wednesday evening; the first Tuesday flight does not provide enough margin for the review.

events.continuity_hook: Retain the selected open-jaw flights, the viable hotel pairings, complete one-way rental totals, drop-charge status, pickup and return hours, Tuesday intercity route, and Wednesday hotel-to-appointment and appointment-to-airport timing.
events.interaction_goal: Verify full hotel and rental costs, confirm the one-way fee and counter hours, and choose the combination that preserves enough time for the Wednesday appointment and flight.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus has chosen a Monday evening arrival in Columbus and a Wednesday evening departure from Cincinnati. He needs one hotel near each appointment and a one-way rental car; one rental quote omits the intercity drop charge, and the lower-priced Cincinnati hotel would add a lengthy drive between the opening check and the airport during the evening commute.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the final flight itinerary, both hotel selections, rental confirmation, complete totals, cancellation deadlines, counter closing time, fuel-stop allowance, and Wednesday appointment-to-airport sequence together as the completed work itinerary.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck dates, traveler details, current totals, and the rental return margin, then book all components if the Wednesday sequence remains feasible.
events.scenario_brief: The selected Columbus and Cincinnati hotels remain available at cancellable one-night rates, and the rental company has confirmed that its updated total includes the intercity drop charge. The Wednesday flight still has availability, but the current fare is higher than the earlier quote and the rental counter closes shortly after the planned return time.
